content: 1. The safety and efficacy of esomeprazole in neonates have not been established. 2. In a juvenile rat toxicity study, esomeprazole was administered as magnesium and strontium salts at oral doses approximately 34 to 57 times the daily human dose of 40 mg, based on body surface area. Increased mortality was observed at the highest dose. At all doses, reductions in body weight, body weight gain, femur weight, femur length, and overall growth were noted. 3. In clinical trials, 1,459 patients aged 65 to 74 years and 354 patients aged 75 years or older received oral NEXIUM. No significant differences in safety or efficacy were observed between elderly and younger patients. However, the possibility of greater sensitivity in some elderly individuals cannot be excluded. 4. There is no FDA guidance on the use of esomeprazole sodium in specific gender populations. 5. There is no FDA guidance on the use of esomeprazole sodium in specific racial populations. 6. There is no FDA guidance on the use of esomeprazole sodium in patients with renal impairment. 7. For adult patients with GERD, no dosage adjustment is necessary in those with mild to moderate hepatic insufficiency (Child-Pugh Classes A and B). For patients with severe hepatic insufficiency (Child-Pugh Class C), the dose should not exceed 20 mg once daily. For adult patients with bleeding gastric or duodenal ulcers and liver impairment, no dosage adjustment of the initial 80 mg esomeprazole infusion is required. For mild to moderate liver impairment (Child-Pugh Classes A and B), a maximum continuous infusion rate of 6 mg/h should not be exceeded. For severe liver impairment (Child-Pugh Class C), a maximum continuous infusion rate of 4 mg/h should not be exceeded. 8. There is no FDA guidance on the use of esomeprazole sodium in women of reproductive potential and males. 9. There is no FDA guidance on the use of esomeprazole sodium in immunocompromised patients. 10. The reconstituted solution of esomeprazole sodium should be stored at room temperature (up to 30°C or 86°F) and administered within 12 hours after reconstitution. If 5% Dextrose Injection is used, administration should occur within 6 hours after reconstitution. 11. For intravenous administration, withdraw 5 mL of the reconstituted solution and administer as an intravenous injection over no less than 3 minutes. The solution can be further diluted to a final volume of 50 mL using 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection, USP, Lactated Ringer’s Injection, USP, or 5% Dextrose Injection, USP. The resulting solution should be administered as an intravenous infusion over 10 to 30 minutes. 12. For risk reduction of rebleeding of gastric or duodenal ulcers in adults, the loading dose of 80 mg should be given over 30 minutes. This dose is prepared by reconstituting two 40 mg vials with 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection, USP.
